title_as_printed: Identifying Alzheimer’s Disease Progression Subphenotypes via a Graph-based Framework using Electronic Health Records

Task_Type.reason: This is subtype discovery. GNN embeddings of longitudinal EHR encounters are clustered (time-series k-means with DTW) into four MCI-to-AD progression subphenotypes, and ML models then predict subphenotype membership (AUROC 0.67-0.70). Inclusion required every patient to convert to AD, so there is no stable-MCI group and no progressive-vs-stable or conversion prediction. The GNN's next-encounter stage forecast (preclinical/MCI/AD) is an auxiliary representation-learning objective whose metrics sit in supplementary eTables. The template restricts T2 to explicit pMCI vs sMCI or MCI-to-AD conversion prediction. The abstract states the aim: 'To identify disease progression subphenotypes in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and AD using electronic health records (EHRs).' (p.3)
Task_Type.quote: patients were required to have a conversion time to the AD of more than six months.

Category.reason: OneFlorida+ EHR data (diagnoses, medications, demographics, vitals).

Validation_Type.reason: Patient-stratified 70/10/20 train/validation/test split, plus 5-fold cross-validated Bayesian search on the training set; single consortium, no external site.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 2,525 MCI/AD patients in the final analysis.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: Our final analysis included 2,525 eligible MCI and AD patients in the cohort.

ADNI_Dependent.reason: OneFlorida+ Clinical Research Consortium EHRs; no ADNI.

notes: Non-peer-reviewed preprint (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-6257332/v1). Coding it T2 would place a subphenotype-membership AUROC (0.67-0.70) among conversion-prediction results.
